title: Practical: Simple Voting System
story: Your school is electing a class president. Voters must be registered, each person votes exactly once, and you need to tally results in real time. A paper ballot box won't cut it — you need a system that prevents double-voting and produces instant results.
why: Combining all three collections with contracts creates a robust voting system — Map for tallying, Set for voter registration, Vec for results display, and contracts for data integrity.
analogy: A voting system is like a polling station with three checkpoints. The registration desk (Set) checks if you're on the voter roll. The ballot handout (Set) checks if you already voted — no getting a second ballot. The ballot box (Map) tallies each vote by candidate. Three checkpoints, three collections, one trustworthy result.
try_it: Add an `ensures` contract: after a valid vote, the total votes cast must equal `has_voted.len()`. Add a `tally` function that verifies the total votes in the Map matches the number of voters in the Set. Try calling `cast_vote` with an unregistered voter — the contract should trap. Try double-voting — the second call should trap.
tips: Use `requires` on the vote function to enforce voting rules at the call site — before the function body runs
Three collections, three jobs: registered (Set), has_voted (Set), votes (Map) — don't try to cram everything into one
The vote counting pattern (get → match → insert with count+1) is the same as word counting from earlier
common_mistakes: Checking `has_voted` but not `registered` — an unregistered person could vote if they haven't voted yet
Using `votes.insert(candidate, votes.get(candidate) + 1)` directly — `.get()` returns Option, can't add to it
Forgetting to add zero-count candidates to the results display — they should show '0 votes', not be missing
